cases.title: Placard 1005
cases.presentation: A tanker on its side on the highway displays a placard: class 2, ID 1005. A faint pungent smell; a motorist downwind is coughing.
cases.question: Best first steps?
options: A: Open the valve to vent pressure.
B: Ask the coughing motorist to come to your ambulance.
C: Approach to read the bill of lading.
D: Stop upwind/uphill at distance, look up 1005 in the ERG yellow pages → guide (orange) → isolation/protective distances (green), isolate and deny entry, METHANE with HazMat request.
cases.explanation: UN1005 is anhydrous ammonia (a toxic-inhalation gas). The ERG workflow — yellow/blue → orange → green — gives the PPE and distances. Ambulatory exposed people should move upwind and disrobe/decon before coming near you.
cases.clinicalPearl: ERG: find the number, read the guide, check the green distances.

cases.title: 200 Wet Commuters
cases.presentation: A sprayer releases an oily liquid in a train station. 200 people exit, many with burning eyes, some vomiting. Fire is setting up a ladder-pipe decon corridor.
cases.question: Your mass-decon priorities?
options: A: Decon in order of arrival only.
B: Wait for Level A suits for everyone.

C: Tell everyone to remove outer clothing immediately; prioritize symptomatic and visibly contaminated for wet decon; separate ambulatory and non-ambulatory lanes; privacy, warmth, keep families together; triage after decon.
D: Send people home to shower.
cases.explanation: Disrobing is decon step one. Visible liquid + symptoms → wet decon. Good crowd management (modesty, warmth, families) keeps people from self-evacuating contaminated.
cases.clinicalPearl: If decon feels humiliating or freezing, people will skip it — design for dignity.
